demographics.trauma_type: Accidentally caused serious injury to another

Maladaptive Strategies.value: Seeing other people that were involved in the event or that look similar
Going to or near the place where the event happened

Memory.value: Remembering the event brings back the same terror I felt at the time
My memories of the frightening event are like a film that plays over and over.
When I remember the event I feel intense guilt

Negative Appraisals.value: My beliefs about how the world works have been completely destroyed
I will never be able to feel normal emotions again
I should have protected others and I failed

Threat.value: Suddenly feeling or acting as if the stressful experience were actually happening again
Having strong physical reactions when something reminded you of the stressful experience
Having strong negative feelings such as fear, horror, anger, guilt, or shame

issues.item: Memory: Verbal Access: I can talk about what happened very easily.
issues.explanation: Within Memory, 'I can talk about what happened very easily' conflicts with highly intrusive, emotionally overwhelming recall ('same terror' on recall and memories replaying over and over). That combination is possible but is clinically hard to reconcile as a stable self-report triad without further nuance, because one item suggests unusually good verbal/intentional access while the others indicate poorly processed, distress-laden traumatic recall.

issues.item: Memory: Terror on Recall: Remembering the event brings back the same terror I felt at the time
issues.explanation: The trigger pattern is not well matched to the trauma type. For accidentally causing serious injury to another person, reminders of the victim are plausible, but sirens and enclosed spaces point toward a survivor-of-accident threat context rather than a perpetration/guilt-centered context. This creates a cross-node mismatch because the profile's appraisals are dominated by global collapse and suicidality, yet there are no guilt/responsibility-related appraisals that would more directly connect to these triggers for this trauma type.

issues.item: Memory: Memory Replay: My memories of the frightening event are like a film that plays over and over.
issues.explanation: 'Avoid enclosed spaces' is weakly coherent with the listed triggers and trauma type. Nothing else in the profile suggests confinement or claustrophobic aspects of the event, so this strategy appears to address a symptom theme not otherwise represented. Given the strong Triggers → Maladaptive Strategies edge, the avoidance strategies should map more directly onto the listed triggers; 'avoid similar people' does, but 'avoid enclosed spaces' does not.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Shattered Beliefs: My beliefs about how the world works have been completely destroyed
issues.explanation: The formulation leaves Threat completely inactive, yet the selected negative appraisals are globally catastrophic and highly threat-laden. For this trauma type, these appraisals suggest a pervasive current-sense-of-threat profile that is not represented elsewhere and sits awkwardly with an entirely inactive Threat node.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Life Not Worth Living: I am not sure my life is worth living anymore
issues.explanation: The negative appraisal set is internally skewed toward extreme global defeat and emotional numbing, but the rest of the profile centers on guilt, victim reminders, and replay/terror memories after causing injury to another. A more coherent appraisal pattern would center on responsibility, moral injury, or fear of causing harm again; the selected items instead imply a different clinical emphasis.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Lost Emotions: I will never be able to feel normal emotions again
issues.explanation: Avoiding enclosed spaces is hard to connect to the other selected items. The triggers are victim reminders, unpredictability, and sirens, and the trauma was accidentally injuring another person. Unless the accident specifically involved confinement, this avoidance target appears clinically disconnected from the rest of the profile and from the formulation, which otherwise links triggers, memory, and guilt-related processes.

For trauma of accidentally causing serious injury to another, reminders of victims and sirens are coherent, but 'unpredictable situations' is a broad trigger more typical of danger-based trauma and is weakly integrated with the rest of this profile, which is dominated by guilt/victim reminders rather than uncertainty or chaos.

issues.item: Maladaptive Strategies: Avoid Enclosed Spaces: Enclosed or confined spaces
issues.explanation: 'Avoid enclosed spaces' does not fit the accident-causing-injury narrative or the other selected symptoms. There are no triggers, memories, appraisals, or threat items suggesting entrapment, confinement, or claustrophobic fear, so this avoidance target appears clinically disconnected.

issues.item: Threat: Hypervigilance: Being superalert or watchful or on guard
issues.explanation: The formulation isolates Threat entirely, and the rest of the profile centers on guilt, victim reminders, and intrusive recollection rather than ongoing external danger. While physical reactivity and flashback-like reliving can fit trauma reminders, generalized hypervigilance/'on guard' implies persistent threat monitoring that is not supported by the accident-specific triggers/appraisals and sits awkwardly with the inactive Threat connections.
